title: The affine w-localization
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and put $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Use $D(f)=\{\mathfrak p\in X:f\notin\mathfrak p\}$ and constructible subsets as in [def-weil-pbc-w-local]. An index is a pair $i=(\mathcal P,(f_E)_{E\in\mathcal P})$, where $\mathcal P$ is a finite partition of $X$ into nonempty constructible subsets and $f_E\in A$ satisfies $E\subseteq D(f_E)$. When $X$ is empty, allow the empty partition. Set
$$B_i=\prod_{E\in\mathcal P}A_{f_E},$$
where $A_f=A[1/f]$ is the localization [def-weil-ring-localization-away]; the product has componentwise ring operations and the diagonal $A$-algebra structure. The empty product is the zero ring.

Give the set of indices the following preorder. For $j=(\mathcal Q,(g_F))$, put $i\leq j$ exactly when $\mathcal Q$ refines $\mathcal P$ and, for every $F\in\mathcal Q$, its unique parent $E\in\mathcal P$ satisfies $F\subseteq E$ and $f_E\mid g_F$ in $A$. There is one arrow for each such relation. The transition $B_i\to B_j$ has $F$-component the projection to $A_{f_E}$ followed by the unique $A$-algebra map $A_{f_E}\to A_{g_F}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property]. Explicitly it sends $a/f_E^n$ to $(a/1)(f_E/1)^{-n}$ in $A_{g_F}$. If $g_F=f_Eh$, then $(h/1)(g_F/1)^{-1}$ is an inverse of $f_E/1$, so the divisibility condition supplies the required unit. For an identity arrow the component map is the identity on $A_{f_E}$ by uniqueness. For $i\leq j\leq k$, each component of the composite and of the direct transition is a map from the same parent localization to the same child localization and agrees on $A$; uniqueness makes them equal.

The index preorder is nonempty (take $\{X\}$ and denominator $1$ when $X\ne\varnothing$, and the empty partition otherwise). A common upper bound of $i,j$ uses the nonempty intersections $E\cap F$ as parts, with denominator $f_Eg_F$. Thus this is a small filtered diagram of commutative $A$-algebras. Define its colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], which exists by [lem-weil-pbc-commutative-algebras-colimits-exist], by
$$A^w=\varinjlim_i B_i.$$
The structural map $A\to A^w$ is induced by the diagonal maps $A\to B_i$. This is an ind-Zariski presentation in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]: every term is a finite product of principal localizations. No assertion about points, connected components or faithful flatness is included in this definition.

blueprint_update.statement:
For a ring $A$, consider finite partitions $\mathcal P$ of
$\operatorname{Spec}A$ into nonempty constructible
[def-weil-pbc-w-local] sets. For each part $E$, choose $f_E\in A$ with
$E\subset D(f_E)$. Refining a partition and multiplying its denominators
gives a directed system of algebras $\prod_{E\in\mathcal P}A_{f_E}$. Define

$$
 A^w=\varinjlim_{(\mathcal P,(f_E))}
          \prod_{E\in\mathcal P}A_{f_E}.
$$

The transition maps are the componentwise localization maps; common
refinements use intersections of parts and products of denominators. This
specifies an ind-Zariski [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra] algebra.
